newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends sharply weaker on U.S. mkt wobble.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends sharply weaker on U.S. mkt wobble.

text.p: The peso relinquished a partial midday recovery to close near weak opening levels on Wednesday as dealers rushed to cover dollar positions ahead of a holiday in Mexico and key U.S. consumer price data on Thursday, traders said.
"There's important U.S. data out tomorrow and we're not working, so dealers want to stay in dollars until Friday,' said one trader.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart closed 4.3 and 3.8 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9070/7.9110 and 7.8920/7.8970 per dollar.
The same-day peso earlier closed 1.0 centavo weaker at 7.8680/7.8730 per dollar.
Mexican financial markets will close on Thursday to commemorate the appearance of the Virgin of Guadalupe. Thursday also sees the release of U.S. consumer price data.
The peso was hit from early trade onwards by rising U.S. long-bond rates and a slide in the Dow Jones, which in turn triggered a sharp slide in Mexican stocks and a consequent demand for dollars.
Yields on the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond climbed to 6.62 percent, compared with 6.49 on Tuesday. The Dow Jones was meanwhile off 1.37 percent at 6,384.83 points.
The leading IPC index of Mexican stocks was off 55.66 points, or 1.68 percent, at 3,251.40 while the foreign exchange market was closing.
Traders said the peso's performance on Friday would greatly depend on the U.S. data.
"It's very difficult to tell how the market will fare on Friday; first we will need to see what tomorrow's figures are like," said a trader.
Traders situated first and second support for the 48-hour peso at 7.92 and 7.96 per dollar, respectively.
